items.title: A founder with a tool is not a founder with a clue
items.excerpt: Dan Maccarone argues AI lets solo founders ship code, design and marketing without a team, but can't supply the judgment to know whether the product is any good - the expertise designers bring.

items.title: AI doesn't care about your job title
items.excerpt: Patrick Neeman says AI exposure runs through the weekly tasks designers do, not the title on their badge, and lays out a way to measure your own exposure across design files, roadmaps and code editors.

items.title: Can you take AI at its word?
items.excerpt: AI agents explain their own work fluently and sometimes wrongly; Dora Czerna argues designers should treat agent self-reports with the same skepticism they learned to apply to human accounts. (Feed carries a teaser only.)

items.title: I built a Claude Code skill that de-slops AI-generated web design
items.excerpt: design-slop-skill is an open Claude Code skill that deterministically detects the 'AI look' in generated pages (huge radii, glassmorphism, red-purple gradients, dark-only, 64px centered heroes) and rewrites them toward human-crafted defaults.

items.title: Figma embraces new AI paradigm but expresses reservations
items.excerpt: Figma co-founder Dylan Field called MCP incomplete and tilted toward big AI labs even as Figma added 20 MCP partners (Notion, ClickUp, Linear) at its India event. Repost of hacks.gr; original reporting by TechCrunch (2026-10-20).

items.title: How to Extract a Website's Design System into DESIGN.md for Your AI Builder
items.excerpt: A workflow for pulling design guidance from a reference site into a DESIGN.md that Lovable, Claude, Codex, Replit or Cursor can follow, so AI-built sites stop looking identical. Note: walkthrough uses the author's tool Preveo (promotional).

items.title: The best a clone can do is tie
items.excerpt: Agents can now rebuild apps from the outside, but every clone is scored against the original, so the best it can do is tie; Builder.io argues for what product and design teams should build instead.

items.title: Europe's Industrial Leaders Reinvent Engineering and Manufacturing With NVIDIA
items.excerpt: At GTC Berlin, Autodesk brings PhysicsNeMo and Warp into NavPack integrated with Autodesk Alias so Bentley designers can predict vehicle performance with simulation-trained AI, and Dassault's CATIA/SIMULIA AI agents design and virtually test car doors.

items.title: AI that understands physics
items.excerpt: Luminary CEO Pete Schlampp explains 'physics AI' - models that predict how a physical product will behave before simulation or test - and how product designers and engineers are starting to use it (vendor-contributed op-ed).

items.title: Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent
items.excerpt: Anthropic opened a waitlist for Claude Duet, a proactive mobile and desktop agent that works across apps, positioned against Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots. Design hook is indirect (general agent).

items.title: Even designers are now using AI to code Windows 11, and Microsoft says "we're only getting started"
items.excerpt: Microsoft's Diego Baca says Windows 11 designers are now making code fixes themselves with AI as Search, Run and Photos are rebuilt in native UI - an in-house design-org AX case. Off-list outlet (no on-list coverage).

items.title: I asked Google Antigravity to build a website, then let Claude Code redesign it
items.excerpt: A hands-on test hands a site built by one AI agent (Google Antigravity) to another (Claude Code) for a full visual redesign, comparing what each gets right about layout and design. Off-list outlet.

items.title: Food Delivery App Apologizes for AI-Generated Menu Photos Showing Bacon Floating in Soda
items.excerpt: Just Eat apologized after inaccurate AI-generated menu photos, including bacon and eggs floating in a soda, appeared on its app - a brand-imagery cautionary tale for AI-made food photography. Off-list outlet; date/image from PetaPixel RSS (page 403s).

items.title: I almost missed the most exciting Photoshop teaser of the year. A new film-inspired filter is coming
items.excerpt: Adobe teased non-destructive, layer-like filters in a future Photoshop plus a light-leak filter and an AI Assistant tool for creating your own filters, shown during its RTX Spark demo. Off-list outlet; overlaps the already-covered Adobe x NVIDIA story.

items.title: Someone turned Draco Malfoy into a girl with AI, and now I need to know what happens next
items.excerpt: Creator Foyege's 'In Another Universe' series moves a long-running fan-art idea into AI animation with cinematic scenes and dialogue; Creative Bloq looks at the design choices behind the viral AI fan series.

items.title: Google Meet gave me facial dysmorphia
items.excerpt: A Creative Bloq writer on Google Meet's 'Touch up your appearance?' prompt and what default AI beauty filters in work tools mean for how we present ourselves. Weak tool-news hook.

items.title: From Travel Clips to a Cinematic Edit with Tati Kapaya | The Brief: Season 2
items.excerpt: Adobe's The Brief S2: creator Tati Kapaya reworks old Egypt travel footage into a short-form edit using Adobe Firefly, Adobe Stock and Premiere. Brand-made content.

items.title: AI Breakthroughs Everyone Missed
items.excerpt: Matt Wolfe rounds up under-the-radar AI releases and research, from AI-generated worlds and games to new voice models and 3D tools.

items.title: Did Google just dethrone OpenAI and Anthropic?
items.excerpt: Fireship test-drives Google's new Gemini 4 Argon against GPT-6 and Claude Opus 5.5 on hands-on build tasks. Model itself launched before the window; this is the in-window hands-on take.
